message.content:
{
  "decision": "APPLY",
  "workflow_yaml": "name: CI
on:
  push:
    branches:
      - main
  pull_request:

jobs:
  CI:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 5
    env:
      TURBO_API: http://127.0.0.1:9080
      TURBO_TOKEN: 61613e87-4749-493b-a569-9a5e15e168cd
      TURBO_TEAM: bezier-react
    steps:
      - name: Checkout
        uses: actions/checkout@v4

      - name: Setup Node.js
        uses: actions/setup-node@v4
        with:
          node-version-file: .nvmrc
          cache: 'yarn'

      - name: Install Dependencies
        run: yarn install

      - name: TurboRepo Local Server
        uses: felixmosh/turborepo-gh-artifacts@v3
        with:
          repo-token: ${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}
          server-token: ${{ env.TURBO_TOKEN }}

      - name: Build
        run: yarn build

      - name: Lint
        run: yarn lint

      - name: Typecheck
        run: yarn typecheck

      - name: Test
        run: yarn test

      - name: Upload Coverage Reports to Codecov
        uses: codecov/codecov-action@v5
        with:
          token: 0a48be00-2768-42b0-b528-7ab854c3db46
",
  "rationale": "The single CI job has no explicit timeout, so a runaway or hung job can consume runner time unbounded. Pattern P-LIT-CUSTOM-TIMEOUT (bound jobs with a custom timeout) is supported: its precondition (representative successful-duration history) is met by the repository's CI history, which shows 5 recent successful runs all completing well under two minutes (slowest about 88s). The matching experiment batch-interactive-three--fb8b16eb65a11508 measured adding timeout-minutes: 5 to a job, reducing median elapsed 41s to 30s (about 26.8%) with all runs still succeeding. Adding timeout-minutes: 5 to the CI job bounds runaway consumption while preserving every build, lint, typecheck, test, and coverage step and all required checks; 5 minutes gives more than 2x headroom over the slowest observed run, so valid slow runs are not expected to exceed it. No permissions, secrets, publishing/deployment operations, or new network access are introduced, and no existing step is removed or altered.",
  "evidence_ids": ["pattern:P-LIT-CUSTOM-TIMEOUT", "experiment:batch-interactive-three--fb8b16eb65a11508"]
}
